body:
VERIFIED against the code (not merely reported).

`cps/readingservices.py` `handle_annotations` wraps the whole capture block in
`except Exception: log.exception(...)` and then, unconditionally, `return
proxy_to_kobo_reading_services()`. Inside, `dispatch_annotation_sync` does check
the commit — `committed = ub.session_commit(); if committed is False: log.error(...);
continue` — but that failure never reaches the response.

So a member that did not persist still produces an upstream-success PATCH answer.

Why that is terminal rather than merely wrong:
- the Kobo uploads a DELTA, so it never re-offers the annotation;
- `checkforchanges` containment deliberately keeps an owned book out of the
  Kobo-cloud download that could otherwise have healed it.

Note the route already has the right instinct one branch up: when ownership
lookup fails it returns 503 *specifically* so "the device does not treat an
uncaptured upload as successful". The same reasoning is not applied to a
capture that was attempted and lost.

The route docstring also claims the path "persists annotations whenever the
PATCH includes content", which is false for this branch.

OPEN QUESTION before fixing — do not guess: what a Kobo does with a non-success
PATCH is UNOBSERVED. Measured hardware behaviour exists for a 503 on the
annotations *GET* (it empties the device's local set), and that must not be
assumed to transfer to PATCH. Needs a device experiment before a fix ships,
otherwise the cure could be worse than the disease.
title: The annotations PATCH is answered success even when a member failed to commit
